newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian tin extends losses after budget duty fall.
newsitem.headline: Indian tin extends losses after budget duty fall.

text.p: Indian tin prices extended losses on Wednesday while copper and zinc remained firm on the metal market, dealers said.
Nickel and lead were weak while aluminium was steady. Tin fell by 300 rupees to 31,500 rupees per quintal amidst continued unloading by stockists as well as sluggish physical demand.

"The Indian finance minister had reduced import duty on tin to 20 percent from 30 percent in the union budget presented on Friday and since then tin prices in the market have lost 2,800 rupees per quintal," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange.
"I think now tin will stabilise at the current level," he added.

Copper and zinc lifted further on the back of scattered arrivals and shortage of ready stock. Copper rose by 50 rupees to 13,350 rupees per quintal while zinc gained by 25 rupees at 7,575 rupees per quintal.

"Prior to the budget Indian importers had curtailed import booking of copper and zinc as they were expecting some reduction in import duty. On this backdrop arrivals of the imported copper and imported zinc remained low," said Parikh.

Nickel fell by 100 rupees to 37,200 rupees per quintal as easing world markets prompted profit-taking. Nickel was up by 100 rupees on Tuesday. Aluminium was steady at 7,400 rupees while lead slid by 25 rupees at 4,525 rupees per quintal on renewed offerings by the state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd.
